rubric: scoring-rubric.md (authored by evaluator; file was missing from repo)

scenarios.name: Discover the API from public documentation
scenarios.note: Documentation site itui.echoit.co.kr does not resolve (DNS ENOTFOUND). README documents 17 components; the package exports 56 component modules. TOKENS.md is high quality but only reachable via the GitHub repo, not from the npm page.

scenarios.name: Install from npm into a fresh project
scenarios.note: npm install succeeded in 47s with 0 vulnerabilities and no peer warnings. Penalised for 98 MB / 16,129 files on disk, 40 MB of shipped sourcemaps, and shipping @types/react + tailwindcss as runtime dependencies.

scenarios.name: Render the first component (time to first pixel)
scenarios.note: The documented JS import path ('import "@echoit/itui.css"' in main.tsx) silently produces a completely unstyled component. Recovered only via the CSS @import path plus installing Tailwind v4 and its Vite plugin.

scenarios.name: Build a realistic form
scenarios.note: Input/Select/Checkbox/Button composed cleanly and typechecked first try. Mixed paradigms: Checkbox uses native onChange while Select uses onValueChange. Error text is not programmatically associated with the input.

scenarios.name: Modal / Dialog flow
scenarios.note: Controlled and uncontrolled both work and Escape closes. But focus is never moved into the dialog, there is no focus trap, and aria-modal is absent: keyboard users tab through the page behind the open modal while the mouse is blocked.

scenarios.name: Data table
scenarios.note: The documented TableRow `disabled` prop has no functional effect: no aria-disabled, pointer-events:auto, and onClick still fires. No aria-sort, no th scope, and sortable headers are not buttons.

scenarios.name: Overlay composition (Popover / Tooltip / Tabs)
scenarios.note: All render correctly. Popover's root is `PopoverRoot` while every sibling family uses the bare name; a different component is also exported as `Popover`. Tooltip requires a Provider, Popover does not, and this is undocumented.

scenarios.name: Toasts
scenarios.note: Works with aria-live=polite. Requires importing `toast` from `sonner`, which is neither a dependency of the consumer app nor a peerDependency — a phantom dependency that resolves only under npm hoisting.

scenarios.name: Theming via design tokens
scenarios.note: Dark mode via .dark works and scopes correctly. TOKENS.md is excellent. But the README's own theming example (--primary, --radius) is a silent no-op; the real tokens (--color-brand, --radius-lg) work perfectly.

scenarios.name: Per-instance customization / className override
scenarios.note: bg-purple-600 and px-10 override successfully but rounded-full silently loses to the library's rounded-lg. Classes are concatenated rather than merged despite tailwind-merge being a dependency, so overrides depend on stylesheet order.

scenarios.name: TypeScript DX
scenarios.note: Strongest area. Named exported types, JSDoc on props, precise union errors, and a 'Did you mean label?' suggestion for a misspelled prop. A 7-file app using ~25 components typechecked clean on the first attempt.

scenarios.name: Accessibility defaults
scenarios.note: Good label association, visible focus rings, sane tab order, aria-busy and role=status. Undermined by the missing dialog focus trap, missing aria-invalid/aria-describedby, missing aria-sort, a non-functional disabled row, and 41 hardcoded Korean UI/a11y strings.

scenarios.name: Error recovery / mistake tolerance
scenarios.note: TypeScript diagnostics are excellent and runtime composition errors are clear. Two failures: the Popover error names the wrong export, and forgetting the stylesheet produces no warning whatsoever.

scenarios.name: Realistic application screen
scenarios.note: A full dashboard (Sidebar, Cards, Table, Dialog, Avatar, Badge, Spinner) composed without fighting the library and rendered correctly in light and dark mode.

scenarios.name: Next.js App Router / SSR
scenarios.note: Importing the package in a Server Component fails the production build with 'TypeError: (0, y.createContext) is not a function'. The dist carries no 'use client' directive. Adding 'use client' to every consumer file works and hydrates cleanly, but this is entirely undocumented.

scenarios.name: Packaging, build output, tree-shaking
scenarios.note: Importing only Button grows the bundle from 190 kB to 974 kB (+229 kB gzip) and pulls in Lexical, sonner, date-fns, calendar and carousel. Adding 24 more components costs only 67 kB more. The README's 'Tree-shakable' claim is false.

criticalBlockers: Next.js App Router: importing the package in a Server Component is a hard production build failure, with no documentation of the 'use client' requirement.
The only documented full-documentation site (https://itui.echoit.co.kr) does not resolve.
The README's documented stylesheet import silently yields completely unstyled components.
Dialog performs no focus management and has no focus trap, locking keyboard and screen-reader users out of modal content.
The documented TableRow `disabled` prop has no functional effect.
Tree-shaking does not work: one Button costs 229 kB gzip, contradicting the README.
evaluatorNotes: test-scenarios.md and scoring-rubric.md were referenced by CLAUDE.md but absent from the repo; both were authored by the evaluator before testing.

Two failures were traced to evaluator error and excluded from scoring: an accidental '@ts-nocheck' string in a comment that suppressed all TypeScript diagnostics, and an initial dark-mode test that used bg-primary instead of the documented bg-background.
npm audit high-severity findings in the Next.js app originate from next/postcss/sharp, not from the target package, and were not counted against it.
